briefing.body: Brent was at about $91.3 on 12 November, down 1.5% on the day and about 14% over the month, from $98.32 on 6 November. IMF PortWatch counted 3 transits through Hormuz on 8 November, against a normal 85 a day. Iran says the US must lift sanctions before the strait can reopen, and talks are deadlocked. LSEG says flows would take time to recover even with a deal.
briefing.short: Brent traded at about $91.3 on 12 November, down 14% in a month. Hormuz stays almost shut while US–Iran talks are deadlocked.
briefing.title: Brent near a two-month low, Hormuz still shut

briefing.body: On 9 November the Ministry of Commerce said the pause on export controls on rare earths and lithium battery technology runs two more months, to 10 January 2027, matching the US-China truce. It gave no other details and no numbered notice yet. Trump and Xi are due to meet at APEC in Shenzhen on 18–19 November. A separate pause, No. 72, ends on 27 November.
briefing.short: China's Commerce Ministry extended the pause on controls on rare earths and lithium batteries by two months, to 10 January 2027.
briefing.title: Beijing extends export-control pause to 10 January

briefing.body: Drewry's index for 5 November put Shanghai–Rotterdam at $3,615/FEU, down 2%, with Shanghai–Genoa stable at $4,166 and the composite down 1% to $4,389. Xeneta's latest weekly figures, from 23 October, are $3,698 to North Europe and $4,442 to the Mediterranean. Analysts at Xeneta's summit on 5 November expect spot rates to fall 30% in 2027 as capacity returns from the Cape.
briefing.short: Drewry's Shanghai–Rotterdam fell 2% to $3,615/FEU on 5 November. Xeneta last had North Europe at $3,698.
briefing.title: Asia–Europe freight eases slightly

briefing.body: Drewry puts 60% of Asia–Europe capacity through Suez, and Alphaliner counts 58% on Far East–North Europe and 70% on Far East–Med. Xeneta counts 467,297 TEU a week on Red Sea routes in October, twice the end-August level but half the level before the crisis. The Gemini ME1 loop returned to Suez from 4 November and the Premier Alliance FE1 from 9 November.
briefing.short: About 60% of Asia–Europe capacity is back in Suez. Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd move their ME1 loop back from 4 November.
briefing.title: More Asia–Europe loops return to Suez

briefing.body: EU officials plan to cap Chinese hybrid imports at 350,000 cars in the first year, rising 6% a year, as a safeguard from 1 December; it is not yet law, and batteries are left out. On 30 October the Commission opened a safeguard probe into hybrid imports from all countries, and on 28 October an anti-dumping probe into the battery material PVDF. It plans to present DiversifyEU, a tool to make firms spread suppliers, around 9 December.
briefing.short: Brussels opened a safeguard probe into hybrid cars from all countries and plans a supplier diversification tool for December.
briefing.title: EU and China: deals, and a tougher line

briefing.body: Germany registered 94,086 battery-electric cars in October, 79.4% more than a year ago and a record 37.0% share. France reached 41% and the Netherlands 55.2%, while Italy stayed at 6.1% and Poland fell to 6.1% from 9.1%. In September the EU share was 29.9% (ACEA).
briefing.short: In October 37% of new cars in Germany were electric, 41% in France and 55% in the Netherlands. Italy and Poland lag at 6%.
briefing.title: Electric cars take a record 37% in Germany

briefing.body: In the week to 10 November ships waited about 2.25 days at Ningbo and 2.28 days at Shanghai, after Super Typhoon Champi closed Ningbo for about 30 hours earlier in the month. Kuehne+Nagel says congestion remains significant and expects it to ease from week 46, so departures for Europe still slip by a few days.
briefing.short: Ships wait about 2.3 days at Ningbo and Shanghai. Kuehne+Nagel expects improvement from week 46.
briefing.title: Ningbo and Shanghai still congested

briefing.body: In the week to 10 November ships waited about 1.87 days at Rotterdam, where the ECT yard is 94% full, 1.79 days at Hamburg (CTH yard 90%), 1.21 days at Bremerhaven (NTB yard 93%) and 1.19 days at Antwerp. Rotterdam was closed by high winds on 23 to 25 October, and dockers at eight Italian ports struck on 30 October.
briefing.short: Ships wait 1.87 days at Rotterdam and 1.79 at Hamburg. Rotterdam's ECT yard is 94% full, Bremerhaven's 93%.
briefing.title: Rotterdam and Hamburg yards near full

briefing.body: DDR4 8Gb contract prices averaged a record $27.50 in October, up 5.77% on September, while MLC NAND was flat at $30.61 (DRAMeXchange). TrendForce expects DRAM contracts up 10–15% and NAND up 15–20% in Q4, and Micron says 2027 and 2028 will be tighter still. Control boards in inverters and onboard chargers cost more.
briefing.short: DDR4 contract prices hit a record in October. TrendForce expects DRAM up 10–15% and NAND up 15–20% in Q4.
briefing.title: Memory crunch hits electronics

briefing.body: Standard LFP prismatic cells from China cost $57.37/kWh in September, 5.1% less than in August (Benchmark). On 4 November InfoLink saw 280/314Ah cells down 0.7% to RMB 0.353/Wh and 100Ah cells down 1.2% to RMB 0.408/Wh, with lithium carbonate down 7.2% to RMB 90,000/t. Cheaper cells mean cheaper battery modules: the stock you hold is worth a little less.
briefing.short: LFP cells from China at $57/kWh in September (Benchmark). InfoLink saw large cells slip to RMB 0.353/Wh on 4 November.
briefing.title: Battery cells get cheaper again

briefing.body: The TAC Index put Hong Kong to Europe at an average $5.31/kg in October, against $4.80 in September. In the week to 2 November the global Baltic Air Freight Index eased 1.1% but stood 22.8% above a year earlier; Hong Kong outbound rose 0.7% and Shanghai 2.8%. Jet fuel costs remain high while Hormuz is restricted. At today's exchange rate $5.31/kg is about €4.79/kg.
briefing.short: TAC Index: Hong Kong to Europe averaged $5.31/kg in October. Global rates were 22.8% above last year in the week to 2 November.
briefing.title: Air freight from Asia stays expensive

briefing.body: Poland is pursuing rail operators, forwarders and customs agents for duties and VAT on imports through Małaszewicze from 2021 to 2026 that an EU probe found fraudulent; on 30 October the rail regulator warned the debts could bankrupt freight operators. Middle Corridor trains rose 125% in January to September, and on 3 November Kazakhstan and Azerbaijan agreed a new Caspian superferry and terminal.
briefing.short: Poland's rail regulator warns customs debts over Małaszewicze imports could bankrupt operators. Middle Corridor trains are up 125%.
briefing.title: China–EU rail: customs claims, new corridor rules

outcomes.body: Washington and Beijing extend their trade truce. China keeps export licences for magnets and battery materials flowing, and buyers in Europe relax.
outcomes.title: The trade truce is extended into 2027

outcomes.body: The summit ends without a new truce. Chinese suppliers of battery modules ask for longer lead times while the licence rules are unclear.
outcomes.title: No deal in Shenzhen

events.title: US and Chinese leaders meet at APEC in Shenzhen

outcomes.body: China's Ministry of Commerce extends the pause on the controls once more. Suppliers keep shipping battery modules and compressors as usual.
outcomes.title: Beijing extends the pause again

outcomes.body: China brings back export licences for permanent magnets and some batteries. Clearance takes weeks, and prices rise across the industry.
outcomes.title: Licences return for magnets and batteries

outcomes.body: Beijing brings back every measure from October 2025. Exports of batteries and of compressors with magnets need licences, and factories cut production for export.
outcomes.title: Chinese export controls return in full

preview.body: The two-month pause on Chinese export controls on rare earths and lithium batteries runs out on 10 January. Much depends on whether the US-China truce holds. Your battery modules, heat pumps and drive units come mainly from China.

choices.desc: Extra orders for battery modules and thermal parts in China, expedited (+3% on price).
choices.label: Build 4 weeks of stock

choices.desc: Urgent audit: €220k and 12 days instead of 28. Hanbit makes battery modules and heat pumps.
choices.label: Fast-track Hanbit (Korea)

choices.desc: No extra cost. You stick with the current plan.
choices.label: Wait for the decision

preview.title: In a week: Beijing decides again on export controls

events.title: Beijing decides again on export controls

outcomes.body: Iran and the US reach a deal, and tankers start leaving the Persian Gulf. Oil gets cheaper and carriers cut their bunker surcharges.
outcomes.title: Strait of Hormuz reopens

outcomes.body: Talks collapse, and there are incidents with tankers in the Gulf of Oman. Brent goes up, and bunker surcharges with it.
outcomes.title: Escalation around Hormuz

events.body: The last big carriers, Evergreen and Zim among them, restore their schedules through the Red Sea. Return legs stop going round the Cape, and the freed-up fleet pushes rates down.
events.title: Suez return completes

outcomes.body: Ministers confirm the easier licensing for rare earths and magnets. The Commission puts new trade defence measures on hold.
outcomes.title: EU and China confirm the agreements

outcomes.body: Brussels finds the progress insufficient and opens an anti-subsidy investigation into parts for electric cars. Provisional duties are possible in about four months.
outcomes.title: Commission probes subsidies for Chinese car batteries and power electronics

events.body: The Commission imposes provisional countervailing duties: 18% on power electronics and 15% on battery modules from China. Goods already in transit pay the duty on import. Competitors raise their prices.
events.title: Provisional duties on Chinese car batteries and power electronics

events.body: Following the American rules on connected cars, the government limits remote access by makers from outside the EU to the electronics in cars on Polish roads. Some fleet customers now want power electronics and batteries made outside China.
events.title: Poland limits remote access to car electronics

outcomes.body: Germany adds a battery health check to the two-yearly car inspection. Owners bring in the cars that fail, and workshops order battery modules.
outcomes.title: The inspection tests every electric car’s battery

outcomes.body: A dispute over the test method delays the new check. Owners put off battery repairs until the rules are clear.
outcomes.title: The battery check is delayed

events.title: Battery checks at the car inspection

outcomes.body: Every new battery module needs a passport. Some Chinese suppliers are not ready, and shipments wait for paperwork.
outcomes.title: Passports start on time

outcomes.body: The Commission gives importers six more months for stock already in Europe. Business carries on as before.
outcomes.title: Brussels allows a grace period

events.body: Beijing closes small lithium mines in Jiangxi over their permits. Lithium and cell prices rise for a second month in a row, and battery modules in warehouses gain value.
events.title: China closes lithium mines

events.body: The expansion of the Dostyk and Altynkol stations finishes on schedule, raising capacity from 18 to 33 trains a day. Border queues disappear, and there is more space on the Caspian ferries.
events.title: Kazakhstan doubles capacity on the Chinese border

events.body: Memory makers put customers on quotas, and electronics companies fight for components. Makers of power electronics cut production.
events.title: Memory chips go on allocation

events.body: A security incident near Bab el-Mandeb closes the southern Red Sea to merchant ships. Carriers stop sailing through Suez and send their ships around Africa.

choices.desc: Your ships that have not reached the strait sail around Africa: about 10–14 days longer and €300 per container.
choices.label: Go around the Cape

choices.desc: The carrier keeps sailing in a protected convoy. €700 per container and a small risk of damage and delay.
choices.label: Sail in a protected convoy

choices.desc: Ships wait for the strait to reopen. No surcharges, but nobody knows for how long.
choices.label: Wait in the Gulf of Aden

events.title: Red Sea closed to shipping again

events.body: Citing security, the government closes the border crossings, including the rail crossing at Małaszewicze. Trains from China are stuck on the Belarusian side.

choices.desc: New orders on the Belarus rail route will go via Suez.
choices.label: Switch the autopilot to sea

choices.desc: Trains will wait for the border to reopen.
choices.label: Stay with rail

events.title: Poland closes its border with Belarus

outcomes.body: The Commission tables its market access instrument and names batteries as a first case. Fleet buyers start asking for modules made outside China, and prices firm.
outcomes.title: Brussels proposes limits on Chinese batteries

outcomes.body: Member states cannot agree on the triggers, and the draft goes back for more work. Buyers carry on as before.
outcomes.title: The draft stalls among member states

events.title: EU market access tool takes shape

outcomes.body: The Commission proposes that firms show they do not rely on one country for critical goods. Fleet buyers start asking for battery modules and inverters from a second source.
outcomes.title: Large buyers must spread their suppliers

outcomes.body: The package sets voluntary targets and reporting only. Buyers carry on as before, and the market calms.
outcomes.title: A soft proposal with voluntary targets

events.title: Brussels proposes limits on single suppliers

label: World as of 12 Nov 2026
lead: The world starts from real news: Brent slips to about $91 as Hormuz talks stay deadlocked, Beijing's export-control pause runs to 10 January, and more Asia–Europe loops return to Suez.

ml.why: Growth pays more than the risks cost: opening countries early wins.
